records.title: Screw propeller and SS Great Britain ocean-steamship integration
records.sourceNativeSummary: The SS Great Britain combined an iron hull, screw propulsion and ocean steam operation in one deep-sea vessel. Its significance is integrative rather than a claim that Brunel invented each component: earlier steamships and propeller experiments existed, while the ship demonstrated a configuration that later became a dominant ocean-vessel pattern.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Paddle steamships were already viable Atlantic vessels; iron+screw integration had to prove reliability/economics at ship scale, and Great Britain itself suffered financial/operational crises.

sources.supports: iron hull, screw propulsion, 1845 Atlantic service and later transition
ship/object archive and operational history

records.title: Suez Canal as interoceanic transport infrastructure
records.sourceNativeSummary: The Suez Canal opened in 1869 after concession, finance, surveying and enormous excavation converted a geographic shortcut into a navigable transport corridor. The consequence came from a whole waterway/port/administrative system and global route reconfiguration, not a novel ship mechanism.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Cape routes remained viable and canal economics/politics were international; construction also relied on coercive corvée labor before later mechanization, so the infrastructure cannot be evaluated only by transit-distance savings.

sources.supports: construction/opening chronology and primary-source navigation
canal authority history and infrastructure chronology

records.title: Indian railway and Indo-European telegraph expansion
records.sourceNativeSummary: The first Bombay–Thana railway opened in 1853 inside a guaranteed-company/state framework, while telegraph links increasingly connected India toward Europe. This was technology transfer plus finance, land, military/administrative priorities and network construction rather than simple replication of a British machine.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Colonial-state and investor objectives were not identical to local welfare; the network's causal boundary includes guarantee finance, extraction/administration and regional labor/material systems.

sources.supports: Great Indian Peninsula Railway formed 1849, guarantee lineage and 1853 Bombay–Thana opening
Indo-European telegraph construction and cross-region technical operations

records.title: Petroleum drilling and the first Pennsylvania oil-field boom
records.sourceNativeSummary: Commercial petroleum shifted from collecting natural seeps to deliberately drilling for a liquid fuel/feedstock. The 1859 Pennsylvania well mattered because it validated a repeatable extraction route into a rapidly scaling oil-field economy, while refining/transport/market demand remained separate complements.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Drake/Bissell did not invent petroleum use, and coal/shale oils remained active illumination competitors; one productive well did not by itself establish petroleum's later dominance.

sources.supports: 1859 well, commercial context and primary sources
well site, drilling and early oil-industry chronology

records.title: Mechanical refrigeration and artificial cold
records.sourceNativeSummary: James Harrison's ether vapor-compression machines converted an existing thermodynamic possibility into commercial ice/refrigeration equipment in Australia during the 1850s; machines then spread internationally. Early ice ventures could still fail because local demand was smaller than plant output, separating technical refrigeration from market fit.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Absorption and other refrigeration routes also existed; Harrison's first commercial arrangements were not uniformly successful despite a working machine.

sources.supports: Harrison compression system, 1856 patent, commercial machines and international diffusion
commercial ice context, failed venture boundary and alternative refrigeration

records.title: Perkin mauveine and synthetic-dye industrialization
records.sourceNativeSummary: Perkin encountered a purple product while pursuing synthetic quinine, recognized a different application, and translated the unexpected chemistry into manufacture. The durable consequence required process scale-up, feedstocks, dyeing tests, capital and fashion demand rather than the accidental observation alone.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The intended quinine route failed; mauveine's value depended on recognizing/reframing the outcome and building an industrial process. Natural dyes remained competitors and later synthetic dyes rapidly superseded mauveine itself.

sources.supports: quinine attempt, mauveine discovery, commercialization and dye-industry lineage
material dye/process history

records.title: Peruvian guano boom: global fertilizer trade, extraction and coerced labor/environmental pressure
records.sourceNativeSummary: Long-known Peruvian guano became a major nineteenth-century global fertilizer commodity as European/American agriculture sought concentrated nutrients. Scale transformed local ecological knowledge into state revenue and global trade while tying extraction/agricultural labor to coercive migration systems.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Guano was not a European discovery and cannot be represented only as a fertilizer-performance improvement; resource depletion, sovereignty, labor abuse and later substitutes were part of the same scaled system.

sources.supports: guano-era economy, Chinese migration/labor and global-commercial linkage
1849 immigration law and captive-labor institutional history

records.title: Sewing-machine convergence and patent-pool commercialization
records.sourceNativeSummary: Howe, Singer, Wilson, Grover/Baker and others contributed different stitch/feed/mechanical elements. By the mid-1850s overlapping patents generated expensive litigation; the 1856 Sewing Machine Combination pooled key rights, allowing firms to redirect effort toward manufacture, marketing and licensing.
records.rivalOrBoundary: No single patent equaled the practical sewing machine, and the pool solved an institutional blocking problem rather than a missing mechanical principle.

sources.supports: Howe patent model, limited early marketing, litigation and 1856 patent pool
Grover/Baker route and patent-pool rationale

records.title: McCormick–Hussey reaper rivalry and agricultural mechanization
records.sourceNativeSummary: Mechanical reaping emerged through competing machines and many improvements rather than one isolated McCormick invention. McCormick's commercial/manufacturing scale became large, while Hussey and other rivals contributed workable cutter/mechanism designs and priority claims.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Later commercial dominance must not be projected backward as exclusive technical priority; the system also depended on draft animals, farm scale, repair/service and complementary harvesting labor/process changes.

sources.supports: 1831 McCormick model, family/Jo Anderson contribution and mechanical harvesting claim
reaper commercialization and rivalry/patent context

records.title: Whitworth precision measurement and standardized screw threads
records.sourceNativeSummary: Whitworth combined precision measurement/machine-tool practice with an 1841 proposed screw-thread form/pitch. Before this, workshops commonly used incompatible local threads; adoption converted a workshop convention into an interoperability substrate.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Standardization did not prove one geometry metaphysically optimal; its value came from coordination/manufacture and coexisted with later competing national/international thread standards.

sources.supports: 1841 thread specification, pre-standard incompatibility and later adoption
precision-measurement/machine-tool substrate

records.title: FitzRoy telegraphic meteorology and storm-warning service
records.sourceNativeSummary: Coastal observations collected by telegraph allowed FitzRoy's Meteorological Office to synthesize weather state rapidly enough to issue national gale warnings from 1861. The service was contested and suspended after his death before public pressure and loss-of-life concerns helped restore it in 1867.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Forecasting models were scientifically disputed and warnings could be ignored or wrong; the service's value depended on observation network, telegraph latency, interpretation and a last-mile warning system rather than a forecast equation alone.

sources.supports: telegraphed observations, 1861 warnings, suspension and 1867 restoration
Royal Charter pressure, scientific contest and warning-service operation

records.title: Maxwell field theory and kinetic-statistical physics
records.sourceNativeSummary: Maxwell's 1864/65 electromagnetic-field paper mathematically reorganized electricity, magnetism and light, while his gas work developed a statistical/dynamical account of molecular motion. These theoretical representations initially had limited direct uptake and required later experiments/instrumentation to establish their wider consequences.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Publication/referee acceptance was not empirical closure, and field/statistical representations did not eliminate all competing mechanical models immediately.

sources.supports: 1864 primary electromagnetic-field manuscript and publication identity
contemporary referee/admission record
1866 kinetic-gas work and later significance

records.title: Nightingale mortality statistics, visual evidence and Army sanitary reform
records.sourceNativeSummary: Nightingale used army/hospital mortality records, comparative tables and visual/statistical communication to argue that much military mortality was preventable through sanitary reform. The work tied data representation to institutional action rather than treating visualization as an end in itself.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Crimean mortality changes had multiple interventions and data-quality problems; the famous diagram is not by itself causal proof. Nightingale's own later colonial-statistics writing explicitly complained that collected data could be incapable of answering practical questions.

sources.supports: 1858 Army mortality tables/diagrams and Royal Commission context
1863 critique of inadequate colonial sanitary statistics and practical-data requirements
Nightingale correspondence/statistics/sanitation archive

records.title: Schleiden–Schwann cell theory
records.sourceNativeSummary: Schleiden's plant work and Schwann's cross-animal comparison helped organize diverse microscopic observations around cellular organization. The theory unified plant/animal biology but included incorrect ideas about cell formation that later microscopy/cell-division research corrected.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A useful organizing unit did not make every proposed generation mechanism correct; improved microscopy and later Virchow/cell-lineage work revised core details.

sources.supports: Schleiden/Schwann cell-theory formulation and later correction
Schwann's role and historical cell-organization context

records.title: Pasteur fermentation and spontaneous-generation experimental program
records.sourceNativeSummary: Pasteur's fermentation work connected specific microorganisms to specific fermentation/spoilage processes and then used controlled exposure/sterility experiments against spontaneous-generation interpretations. The program combined industrial pressure, microscopy, culture/handling technique and rival causal models.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Pasteur was not the first to oppose spontaneous generation or use heating for preservation; his contribution included experimental causal explanation and a broader microbial research program rather than sole origin of every practice.

sources.supports: fermentation, minority microorganism view, spontaneous-generation dispute and 1865 wine process
Pasteur's 1866 wine/fermentation primary work
industrial problem, fermentation mechanism and prior-practice boundary

records.title: Karlsruhe/Cannizzaro atomic-weight coordination to 1869 periodic classification
records.sourceNativeSummary: Chemists entered the 1860 Karlsruhe congress with incompatible atom/molecule definitions and atomic weights; the formal meeting did not simply settle them. Cannizzaro's pamphlet, circulated after the sessions, helped stabilize weights used by Meyer/Mendeleev and other classification efforts, culminating in competing periodic systems by 1869.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Conference existence did not create consensus, and Mendeleev was not the only periodic classifier. Representation quality depended on improved atomic-weight coordination plus later prediction/confirmation of missing elements.

sources.supports: Karlsruhe dispute, pamphlet diffusion and atomic-weight standardization
parallel Meyer/Mendeleev classification and Karlsruhe influence
multiple 1860s periodic systems and atomic-weight precondition

records.title: South Devon atmospheric railway: deployed propulsion abandoned after coupled maintenance failure
records.sourceNativeSummary: Brunel's South Devon line physically operated atmospheric trains in 1847–48 using stationary pumps and a slotted pipe with continuous leather seal. The system could achieve useful speeds, yet coupled sealing, maintenance, pumping/coordination and operating costs made sustained operation unattractive and it returned to locomotives.
records.rivalOrBoundary: This was not a paper failure: a working deployed system was abandoned. The failure therefore bears on lifecycle/maintenance economics, not on whether atmospheric propulsion could move trains at all.

sources.supports: 1847 operation, leather-seal mechanism, technical difficulties and September 1848 abandonment
operation, seal/coordination friction and cost-driven abandonment

records.title: Babbage Analytical Engine: programmable architecture without completed operational machine
records.sourceNativeSummary: After the Difference Engine stalled, Babbage designed a much more general punched-card Analytical Engine with separate store and mill and worked on it for decades. Only trial pieces were built; funding, manufacturing scope and project integration never converged into the intended operational machine in his lifetime.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Later recognition or construction of related Difference Engine designs does not prove the Analytical Engine was tractable under Babbage's contemporary project world. Rich architecture and future influence are distinct from completed capability.

sources.supports: Analytical Engine architecture, noncompletion, funding/manufacturing history and archive
Lovelace notes, punched-card design and incomplete physical engine

records.title: Great Eastern: extreme-scale steamship engineering without sustainable original commercial model
records.sourceNativeSummary: Great Eastern pushed iron steamship size, capacity and long-range engineering far beyond contemporary commercial practice. The ship proved many scale capabilities but its intended passenger/commercial model struggled; later it found a very different high-value role as a cable-laying platform.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Technical scale achievement did not imply product-market fit. A commercially disappointing artifact could still become uniquely useful when a different problem—ocean cable carrying capacity—appeared.

sources.supports: ship scale, commercial history and later cable-laying use
Great Eastern's 1866 Atlantic-cable role

records.title: Goodyear–Hancock independent vulcanized-rubber routes
records.sourceNativeSummary: Natural rubber's heat/cold instability created a real material problem. Goodyear in the United States and Hancock in Britain independently developed sulfur/heat treatments that produced much more stable rubber, with different patent/geographic paths and evidence exchange.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Priority is not reducible to one global 'inventor': Hancock saw Goodyear-cured samples but independently investigated sulfur and filed a British patent before Goodyear did there. The process also generated multiple material variants rather than one exact recipe.

sources.supports: Goodyear 1839 vulcanization properties and material adoption
Hancock 1842–43 investigation, patent and vulcanite route
independent Goodyear/Hancock history and vulcanized-rubber material capability

records.title: Adams–Le Verrier independent Neptune prediction and observational confirmation
records.sourceNativeSummary: Unexpected Uranus motion led Adams and Le Verrier independently to infer an unseen planet from gravitational theory. Le Verrier communicated a sufficiently actionable sky position to Galle, who observed Neptune in 1846; Adams' route did not secure the same timely observational follow-through.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Two similar mathematical predictions did not have equal consequence because communication/evaluator action differed. Prediction and physical observation remain separate events, and later priority credit was institutionally contested.

sources.supports: independent Adams/Le Verrier predictions, Galle observation and priority history
contemporary prediction/publication lineage for later primary audit

records.title: Semmelweis chlorinated hand disinfection: strong local mortality evidence with delayed institutional adoption
records.sourceNativeSummary: Semmelweis compared two maternity clinics, inferred a transferable contaminant after a colleague's autopsy-related death and introduced chlorinated-lime hand disinfection in 1847; mortality fell sharply. The intervention remained resisted because mechanism, professional implications, publication style and theory fit were contested.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Strong observational/intervention evidence did not instantly settle causal theory; animal experiments were ambiguous, and Semmelweis' own dissemination/institutional relations complicated adoption.

sources.supports: clinic comparison, 1847 intervention, mortality drop and professional resistance
animal-experiment ambiguity and contemporary causal challenge
historical mortality/intervention reconstruction

records.title: Mendel pea inheritance experiments and long delayed recognition
records.sourceNativeSummary: Mendel ran structured hybridization experiments through the 1850s–60s, presented the results locally in 1865 and published in 1866. The quantitative inheritance regularities received little immediate disciplinary uptake and became widely recognized only decades later when a compatible genetics problem/evidence community existed.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The later 'father of genetics' narrative should not imply nineteenth-century biologists ignored an obviously complete modern theory; terminology, research questions, distribution and later reinterpretation all differed.

sources.supports: 1854–64 experiments, 1865 presentations and 1866 publication
nine-year experiments, 34 pea varieties and publication chronology

records.title: British railway gauge war, Gauge Commission and 1846 standard constraint
records.sourceNativeSummary: Competing broad and standard gauges embedded different engineering/economic claims in expanding railway networks. As interconnection grew, break-of-gauge created network costs that individual-line optimization did not internalize; Parliament imposed a geographic gauge constraint in 1846 after commission/debate.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The adopted standard need not be interpreted as proving broad gauge technically inferior in every local dimension. Coordination cost and installed-base/network effects changed the decision boundary.

sources.supports: contemporary parliamentary gauge debate
1846 Gauge Act legal constraint

records.title: International Telegraph Union: cross-border equipment, operations and tariff coordination
records.sourceNativeSummary: Rapid international telegraph expansion left incompatible bilateral/regional rules, equipment and tariffs. Twenty states met in Paris in 1865 and created the International Telegraph Union plus common international regulations for service, technology and accounting.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The ITU did not centralize all national telegraph authority; it standardized the cross-border interface while states retained domestic control and later conferences repeatedly revised operational rules.

sources.supports: 1865 convention, equipment/tariff/service rules and treaty boundary
20-state conference and coordinated international regulations
pre-1865 fragmented agreements and convergence pressure

records.title: Lister antiseptic surgery: a surgical infection-safety correction built on carbolic disinfection
records.sourceNativeSummary: Lister applied carbolic-acid antisepsis to wounds and surgical practice in the 1860s, publishing the antiseptic principle in 1867. The method evolved materially—crusts, dressings, sprays and later simplification—rather than one frozen protocol becoming permanent.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Early antiseptic practice was cumbersome and germ transmission details were still developing. Later abandonment of specific sprays/dressings did not invalidate the broader infection-control objective.

sources.supports: Lister's 1867 antiseptic-principle paper provenance
1867 antiseptic treatment illustrations
1860–69 ward practice and evolving carbolic treatment

records.title: Mines and Collieries Act 1842 after underground labor/safety inquiry
records.sourceNativeSummary: A Royal Commission documented extremely young children and women working underground, creating political pressure for the 1842 Act that prohibited underground work for women/girls and boys under ten. Later mine inspection laws show that prohibition and effective safety oversight were different institutional steps.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The Act addressed specified labor practices but did not solve mine accidents or education; inspection capacity expanded only later, so statute existence is not equivalent to comprehensive worker safety.

sources.supports: Royal Commission evidence and Act provisions
contemporary Commission evidence and legislative pressure
1842 provisions and later inspection/regulation chronology

records.title: Gutta-percha insulation: Southeast Asian material supply as a hidden submarine-telegraph substrate
records.sourceNativeSummary: Gutta-percha, a Southeast Asian tree gum introduced into British industry in the 1840s, provided unusually useful underwater electrical insulation and was manufactured around early submarine cables. A globally extracted material became an invisible enabling substrate for European/Atlantic communication infrastructure.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The material was not sufficient for durable cables: the unarmoured 1850 Dover–Calais cable failed almost immediately and had to be redesigned; extraction/supply and ecological consequences sit outside a purely electrical account.

sources.supports: Gutta Percha Company cable, insulation and first-night failure
1850 cable construction and 1851 successor boundary
Singapore/Malay gutta-percha origin and global telegraph linkage
